question: During an exchange of views on the EU’s forest strategy at the meeting of the European Parliament’s Committee on Agriculture on 24 January 2024, the Commission reported on the efforts currently being made on forest-related legislation. The Commission mentioned a forthcoming legislative proposal on sustainable forestry, the aim of which is to establish benchmarking to improve the way in which the concept of sustainable forestry is put into practice. 1.
How far has the Commission got with its work on the legislative proposal concerned?
What indicators have been used and what are they based on?
How have different forest types in Europe been taken into account in the legislative proposal?
answer: There is no pending or planned legislative proposal on sustainable forestry. A legislative proposal on a framework for monitoring resilient European forests was published by the Commission on 22 November 2023 (1) and is currently discussed by the co-legislators. The proposal aims to ensure collection and availability of data and information that underpin sustainable forestry in a changing climate.

The indicators in this proposal have been selected to reflect all functions of the forest and are based on the impact assessment (2) and consultations with national experts under the ad hoc expert sub-group under the Standing Forestry Committee. They have been defined on the basis of the forest monitoring that is already being carried out in the Member States.

European Forest Type as described in the European Environment Agency’s Technical report No 9/2006 is one of the indicators in the proposal. It entails categorisation of forest into 14 categories following established methodologies (3).

COM (2023) 728. https://environment.ec.europa.eu/publications/proposal-regulation-forest-monitoring-framework_en Giannetti, F. et al. European Forest Types: toward an automated classification. Annals of Forest Science 75, 6 (2018).
